summary.text: A 12-year-old girl presented with a 12-hour history of lower abdominal pain. Vital signs were temperature 36.4 °C, heart rate 100 beats/min and respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, with mid-lower abdominal tenderness without rebound or a palpable mass. Initial point-of-care ultrasound showed an anechoic pelvic area interpreted as physiologic ascites; a rectal enema, given for a history of constipation, produced a bowel movement and relief, and she was discharged.

She returned five hours later with recurrent pain and vomiting. Repeat ultrasound showed an enlarged anechoic area, and prevoid and postvoid scans showed that the presumed bladder was a 90-mm cystic lesion without septations or solid components. A pelvic reproductive-organ ultrasound showed a normal left ovary with the right ovary not visualized, and contrast-enhanced CT showed an enlarged right adnexa with a whirlpool sign.

Emergency surgery confirmed a 360° right ovarian torsion, and detorsion with ovarian preservation and cystectomy was performed. She recovered uneventfully and was discharged on hospital day 4. Pathological examination revealed a serous cystadenoma.

summary.text: An eight-year-old girl presented with a three-day history of lower abdominal pain and vomiting. Vital signs were body temperature 38.5 °C, heart rate 120 beats/min and respiratory rate 20 breaths/min. Physical examination revealed diffuse abdominal tenderness, more pronounced on the left, without rebound tenderness or a palpable mass.

Radiology-performed ultrasound showed a 110-mm cystic lesion superior to the bladder producing the double-bladder sign, containing calcification and small peripheral cysts (daughter cyst sign), with a normal right ovary. Color Doppler showed partial flow within the enlarged left ovarian lesion with leftward uterine deviation. Contrast-enhanced CT showed a large cystic lesion with calcification and fat and an enlarged left ovary with follicles. Emergency surgery confirmed a 630° left ovarian torsion, and detorsion was performed with ovarian preservation and cystectomy. Pathological examination confirmed a mature teratoma.

summary.text: A three-year-old girl with four days of abdominal pain and vomiting was referred after an ultrasound at a previous hospital suggested an ovarian tumor. Temperature was 38.5 °C, heart rate 140 beats/min, respiratory rate 24 breaths/min and blood pressure 80/57 mm Hg, with abdominal distension and no definite tenderness, rebound tenderness or palpable mass.

Radiology-performed ultrasound showed a 58-mm cystic lesion superior to the bladder producing the double-bladder sign, with solid components and a fluid-fluid level; the right ovary was normal and the left was not visualized. MRI showed a large cystic lesion, a normal right ovary and signal indicating intralesional fat, highly suggestive of left ovarian torsion due to a teratoma. Emergency surgery confirmed a 360° left ovarian torsion, and detorsion was performed with ovarian preservation and cystectomy. Pathological examination confirmed a mature cystic teratoma.

summary.text: A 14-year-old girl presented a few hours after the onset of abdominal pain and vomiting. Temperature was 36.2 °C, heart rate 78 beats/min and respiratory rate 20 breaths/min. She had lower abdominal distension and appeared to be in severe pain with a grimacing expression, and no palpable mass was detected.

Radiology-performed ultrasound showed a 111-mm cystic lesion superior to the bladder producing the double-bladder sign, with the normal left ovary posterior to it and a mass with a daughter cyst sign superior to the lesion on the right side. With the clinical findings, these features strongly suggested right ovarian torsion. Emergency surgery confirmed a 360° right ovarian torsion, and detorsion was performed with ovarian preservation and cystectomy. Pathological examination revealed an immature teratoma.

summary.text: A five-year-old girl presented with a six-day history of abdominal pain. Temperature was 36.7 °C, heart rate 84 beats/min and respiratory rate 20 breaths/min. Examination revealed a firm, elastic mass in the right lower abdomen with localized tenderness over the same area.

Radiology-performed ultrasound showed a 117-mm cystic mass superior to the bladder on the right side producing the double-bladder sign and depicting a daughter cyst sign. CT showed a cystic mass containing calcification and fat, findings consistent with right ovarian torsion due to a teratoma. Emergency surgery confirmed a 360° right ovarian torsion, and detorsion was performed with ovarian preservation and cystectomy. Pathological examination confirmed a mature teratoma.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; all eight figure images were inspected separately in visual.json.

The Discussion statement that the structure closest to the pubic symphysis might have been recognized as the bladder (Figure 8) is a counterfactual teaching point and is not recorded as a patient finding.
No dates, laboratory values, medications, or follow-up after discharge are reported for any case; orders between investigations are recorded only where the text states them.
Immature teratoma (Case 4) is not stated to be malignant in the case text and is recorded as a condition, not an oncology tumor.
Pre-operative imaging suspicions (suggested or consistent with torsion) are kept as possible/provisional separately from the surgically confirmed torsion.
